pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK; test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' asserts all seeded rows are 0 and that 2 is rejected.
The item() renderer in src/index.js adds '★ ' for starred rows; test 'AC-2' checks the exact list with one starred item.
The starred view filters WHERE starred = 1 ORDER BY id; test 'AC-3' stars 3 and 1 and expects id order.
Test 'AC-4' checks / and /?show=all give the full list in id order.
Test 'AC-5' checks the exact anchors for both views.
Object.hasOwn guard returns 400; test 'AC-6' covers Starred, none, empty and __proto__, and checks there is no <li>.
traffic/routes.json contains /?show=starred; test 'AC-7' asserts it. The traffic checker script now accepts the query, with a test in tests/traffic-config.test.sh.

findings.what: The README mentions ?show=starred but not the ★ marker or the 'Starred only' / 'All items' links, and says nothing about the 400 on other show values.
findings.fix: Add one sentence on the ★ marker, the view links and the 400 for unknown show values.

lenses.note: The spec is present, with a dated go. The change matches its decisions: starred items keep their place, and the view is a query parameter.
All 7 acceptance items are met. All 4 state-table rows have tests that check the list, message and link. The spec was added in the same commit as the implementation, with no later edits.
Tests assert rendered behaviour and would fail on broken code. I did not run them here; CI runs them. The traffic fake-app change is disclosed and is not a loosening.
The README is slightly incomplete (see the low finding) but not wrong.
The view lookup uses Object.hasOwn, so __proto__ is safe. The SQL is built only from fixed view strings. The checker regex change only permits ?.
Titles are still escaped. The show value is never interpolated into SQL or HTML. No planted instructions found.
The diff changes only a minimal server-rendered HTML list with no UI files such as CSS or components.
The diff has no UI files (no CSS or components), and no browser is available.
The title is under 72 characters. The claims match the diff, including the disclosed traffic-checker and fake-app changes.
